problem_type: Anchored canvas overlay placed over fixed chrome (canvas bottom docks, the node's own toolbar/label row) because its usable area and above-clearance were not measured from the real obstacles
symptom: 2026-09-21 screenshot tests/ux/shots/prompt-translate/04-zh-image-icon-and-result.png: an image node's generation composer opened toward the bottom-left of the canvas and its footer (variant/parameter chips, count, generate) sat under the zoom toolbar and the 'Timeline 0 clips' pill; on main the walkthrough measured 4 to 7 footer-control/dock intersections at 1280x933 and at the 1100x720 minimum window. Follow-up A (same branch, same class): a composer flipped ABOVE its node overlapped the node's floating toolbar by 8px (walkthrough: card bottom 268, toolbar top 262 at zoom 1; zh and en). Follow-up found while verifying: at 1100x720 when neither side fits, the card was shortened below its fixed content so the footer spilled out of the card onto the zoom bar (-2px). Follow-up C: when the card was pressed to its minimum (flipped above at 1280x933, and 1100x720), the 'Generation mode' tabs lived inside the references scrollport, which was squeezed to 1-28px: the tabs showed only their lower half and the en label collapsed to a line; tabs were not hittable (walkthrough: scrollport 516-517 vs mode bar 516-582). Also present on origin/main at the default position and at 1100x720 (probe run on 1d7c1e2a5), so pre-existing, not introduced by this branch.
direct_cause: useComposerViewportPlacement passed resolveAnchoredPlacement a stage that was only inset by a 12px margin and the left rail; the bottom docks (CanvasNavigationStack, the timeline pill, the collapsed Nomi dock, the batch dock, the timeline mini preview) are drawn above the React Flow viewport (the composer lives inside the transformed viewport, so no z-index can lift it over them) and were never subtracted, so 'below fits' was judged against stage.bottom. For the flipped side, aboveClearance was toolbar HEIGHT + 18, but the toolbar sits 40 canvas units above the node (72 with an inline status) over the label row; that band was never reserved. When both sides were short the card height went to the available space even if that was below the prompt+footer minimum. The mode bar was rendered inside the references scrollport, and the scrollport had no floor, so the fixed-height measurement treated both as fully compressible; the placement ResizeObserver also only watched the outer wrapper, so a newly mounted reference row inside a height-capped card never triggered a re-measure.
class_root: The bottom-dock registry (workspaceBottomDocks.ts, data-canvas-bottom-dock) had one consumer for floating canvas overlays (the multi-select toolbar, with a private copy of the usable-bottom rule); the 2026-09-10 drift fix removed all obstacles from composer placement, including fixed chrome, and only the left rail was re-added. There was no single usable-bottom rule that every anchored canvas overlay reads. The same shape applies above the node: what the node itself draws outside its top edge (toolbar, label row, inline status) was approximated from one element's height instead of measured.
affected_population: Every generation composer (image, video, audio, text and plugin nodes) whose horizontal span crosses a bottom dock: default insertion position at common window sizes, nodes near the bottom-left, and the 1100x720 minimum window, in zh and en
entry_points: Selecting a node opens its composer below/above it (NodeGenerationComposer -> useComposerViewportPlacement -> resolveAnchoredPlacement)

external_sources.purpose: Flip/shift semantics already adopted by anchoredPlacement: the boundary is the usable clipping area, which is exactly where fixed chrome must be subtracted

invariants: An anchored canvas overlay's rectangle never intersects any element that declares data-canvas-bottom-dock and shares its horizontal span; the usable bottom for a horizontal span is computed by exactly one function (resolveUsableBottomAboveDocks)
A flipped composer ends a gap above the highest node-owned chrome (toolbar, label row, inline status) measured from real rects
The card is never resolved shorter than its fixed content (padding, prompt minimum, footer); when that does not fit, it shifts within the usable stage and may cover the anchor, never the chrome
The generation-mode row and the first reference row are fixed content: they count toward the card minimum and are never clipped by the references scrollport

door_reduction.why_not: Generated by node scripts/door-map.mjs resolveUsableBottomAboveDocks collectBottomDockElements collectBottomDockRects data-canvas-bottom-dock aboveClearanceFromNodeChrome data-node-label-row data-node-floating-toolbar data-node-composer-mode-bar referenceScrollportHeight ModeBar. Writers are elements declaring themselves as chrome or fixed rows (marker discipline); readers are the dock-avoiders, the two floating overlays and the one placement owner that measures fixed content. Each rule has one implementation.

generality_proof: The rule no longer lives in a caller: resolveAnchoredPlacement derives the usable bottom from bottomDocks after it fixes the horizontal span, and the only producer of those rects is collectBottomDockElements over the workspace scope. Any new dock that declares the marker, any window size, any node kind, and both locales flow through the same function; the class test sweeps anchors across the whole stage against the real measured dock band.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Single usable-bottom rule for a horizontal span over the bottom-dock registry
Anchored overlay geometry: width/left first, then usable bottom from bottomDocks, then below/above flip inside that usable stage
Above-side clearance = node top minus the highest measured node-owned chrome top
References scrollport never drops below its floor (first reference row); the floor and the mode row are part of the measured fixed height that becomes minHeight

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Collects bottom docks from the owner each recompute and folds their rects into the per-frame signature; walkthrough composer-overlap-and-fast-typing: 0 intersections at default, bottom-left, and 1100x720 in zh and en
Private resolveUsableBottom deleted; now calls resolveUsableBottomAboveDocks; selectionToolbarPlacement.test.ts unchanged and green
Anchored inside the Agent panel, not over the canvas stage; passes no bottomDocks so its placement is byte-identical
Sits above its node; the composer reserves its height as aboveClearance and there are no top docks
Measured as node-owned chrome; walkthrough asserts no card/label-row intersection in zh and en
Mode bar moved out of the references scrollport into its own card row; walkthrough asserts it is fully inside the card, not intersecting the prompt, tabs hittable, zh/en, flipped and 1100x720

recurrence.reason: Third composer-vs-chrome placement defect (09-09 obstacles, 09-10 drift removal re-exposed the left rail, now the bottom band). Any new dock or overlay can repeat it unless the usable area has one owner.
same_class_scan: rg data-canvas-bottom-dock src -> 5 declaring docks, 3 avoiders
rg resolveAnchoredPlacement src -> composer placement and Agent context popover
rg resolveUsableBottom src -> private copy in selectionToolbarPlacement.ts (deleted)
rg getUnobstructedComposerSpaceBelow src -> test-only orphan from the removed obstacle system (deleted)

prevention.invariant: Floating canvas overlays compute their usable bottom only through resolveUsableBottomAboveDocks over the declared docks; flipped overlays reserve the measured node-owned chrome; the card never drops below its fixed content height; the mode row and first reference row are fixed content counted in the card minimum
prevention.failure_mode: When neither side can hold the natural height the card is shortened inside the usable stage (prompt and references scroll); it never extends into a dock
prevention.strategy: Move the rule to the dock registry owner, make resolveAnchoredPlacement take the dock rects, and delete the second copy and the orphaned helper

legacy_paths.rationale: Deleted the selection toolbar's private resolveUsableBottom and the test-only getUnobstructedComposerSpaceBelow left over from the removed obstacle system (the orphan lived in src/workbench/generationCanvas/nodes/nodeSizing.ts); deleted toolbarClearanceInCanvasUnits (height-based clearance) and TOOLBAR_CLEARANCE_GAP from useComposerViewportPlacement.ts; the references section no longer renders ModeBar (it renders only under section="mode" or the unused 'all')

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: React Flow renders the composer inside its transformed viewport, which is why chrome cannot be solved by stacking order; the usable-area rule is application geometry

migration: No persisted state; placement is recomputed on every open.
residual_risks: Layout-rule choice: the composer yields to the chrome (shortens or flips) instead of chrome fading. The chrome-fades alternative was rejected because the composer lives inside the React Flow transform and cannot sit above the chrome, and hiding the zoom bar and timeline pill while a node is selected removes working controls; recorded in the report for the user to overrule
When the node itself sits inside the dock band at the minimum window, the card may be shortened to its minimum usable height; the walkthrough covers 1100x720 only

When the fixed content cannot fit on either side (1100x720 with a 340px node) the card covers the lower part of its own node; accepted Floating UI shift behavior, the node image stays partly visible and the composer stays fully usable

With the larger fixed minimum (mode row + one reference row + prompt + footer), at the default insertion position and at 1100x720 the card now covers the lower part of its own node instead of hiding the reference row (screenshots 00, 02, 07)

invariant_owner_layer.why: The dock registry already owns which elements are docks; the usable-bottom rule belongs next to it so every overlay reads the same answer
